report.summary: Chunk 2/4 of harness.py: implements tier-1 eval loop, whole-repo text, BM25 retrieval, and arms A/B/C comparison. Defines _whole_repo_text, _target_query, _repo_chunks, _bm25_tokenize, _bm25_scores, _bm25_context, eval_task_arms, constant _DEFAULT_MODEL_CAP_TOKENS.
risks: _whole_repo_text | medium | docstring claims `cap_chars=None` walks entire repo untruncated; code does that but `_DEFAULT_MODEL_CAP_TOKENS * 4` multiplier for cap is arbitrary and not documented. | Clarify why 4x token cap is used for character cap.

_bm25_context | medium | docstring says single best-ranked chunk always included even if exceeds budget; code checks `if picked and total + t > budget_tokens:` but first chunk bypasses `picked` check because `picked` is empty. This matches docstring but logic is implicit. | Confirm behavior via test with first chunk over budget.

eval_task_arms | medium | Docstring claims NEVER RAISES, but try block only catches ValueError/OSError; other exceptions (e.g., KeyError, TypeError) would propagate. | Add broader exception handling or document uncovered exceptions.
todos: Verify that `_DEFAULT_MODEL_CAP_TOKENS * 4` is correct for character cap.
Ensure `eval_task_arms` truly never raises by catching all exceptions or explicitly documenting uncaught ones.
Add test for `_bm25_context` when first chunk exceeds budget.

handoff.purpose: Implements tier-1 evaluation loop, whole-repo text retrieval, BM25 retrieval, and deterministic A/B/C arm comparison.

symbols.name: _whole_repo_text
symbols.note: Walks repo directory, reads files, concatenates with headers. Returns (text, truncated). cap_chars=None means untruncated.

symbols.name: _target_query
symbols.note: Generates BM25 query fallback from target string.

symbols.name: _repo_chunks
symbols.note: Splits repo into extractable units (functions/classes) for BM25 retrieval.

symbols.name: _BM25_TOKEN_RE
symbols.note: Regex for tokenizing BM25: matches identifiers.

symbols.name: _bm25_tokenize
symbols.note: Tokenizes text into lowercase words matching identifier pattern.

symbols.name: _bm25_scores
symbols.note: Computes Okapi BM25 scores for query against pre-tokenized docs.

symbols.name: _bm25_context
symbols.note: Top-k BM25 retrieval up to budget_tokens. Always includes top chunk even if over budget.

symbols.name: _DEFAULT_MODEL_CAP_TOKENS
symbols.note: Default token cap for Tier-2 model context, set to 120,000.

symbols.name: eval_task_arms
symbols.note: Deterministic A/B/C comparison for one task. Returns dict with recall and token counts. NEVER RAISES (catches ValueError/OSError).

claims.text: No top-level blended recall/compression: see ``by_provenance`` for the honest, per-provenance-tier numbers.
claims.why: by_provenance is returned but its implementation is not in this chunk.

claims.text: ``tier == "quarantine"`` tasks are counted in ``n_quarantine_tasks`` and reported inside ``by_provenance``, but never inside a go/no-go figure.
claims.why: by_provenance implementation not in chunk; n_quarantine_tasks is computed as n - n_primary.

claims.text: A single unresolvable task (bad ``repo`` label, or a target no longer in the index -- the quarantined-mint-task crash this guards against) is caught here too, not just inside ``eval_task_tier1``: this loop resolves the repo/builds the index ITSELF (for the cross-task index cache) before calling ``eval_task_tier1``, so that resolution step needs its own guard.
claims.why: Loop resolves repo and builds index cache; try/except catches ValueError/OSError and appends error row.

claims.text: ERRORED rows land in both ``per_task`` (never silently dropped -- "a degraded measurement is reported, never silent") and the dedicated ``errored`` list, and are excluded from ``by_provenance`` (every mean/recall/compression aggregate) -- see ``_by_provenance``'s docstring.
claims.why: errored list built from per_task where 'error' in t; healthy excludes errored rows; by_provenance uses healthy.

claims.text: ``n_tasks``/``n_primary_tasks``/``n_quarantine_tasks`` remain simple total-attempted counts over label alone (unaffected by error status, and therefore byte-identical to before this existed for any store with zero errored tasks); ``n_errored_tasks`` is new and additive.
claims.why: n_tasks = len(per_task) includes all tasks; n_primary counts based on label_tier; n_quarantine = n - n_primary; n_errored_tasks additive.

claims.text: Refused BEFORE the repo is resolved, not only inside eval_task_tier1: this loop does its own resolution for the index cache, and a correctness task is not required to carry anything this harness can resolve. The refusal must not depend on the task being sliceable.
claims.why: Loop checks is_correctness_task before resolution and appends _correctness_task_row.

claims.text: FOCUS-WITHHELD (lane A1): the fence fail-closed on the task's own focus file -- not a resolution error (excluded above), not a recall outcome either. Excluded from `healthy` (therefore from every mean/miss count in by_provenance) same as errored rows, and separately counted/named so it is reported, never silently folded into either a pass or a miss.
claims.why: Focus-withheld logic references _is_focus_withheld and _focus_withheld_row which are not in this chunk.

claims.text: ``cap_chars=None`` (the new default) walks the ENTIRE repo untruncated -- the TRUE size of the baseline.
claims.why: Code when cap_chars is None does not truncate; returns full concatenation.

claims.text: Pass an int to cap it (what Tier 2 actually hands a model). Returns (text, truncated); ``truncated`` is always False when uncapped.
claims.why: When cap_chars is not None, code truncates block and sets truncated=True; when None, truncated remains False.

claims.text: Same source-file universe as ``_whole_repo_text``.
claims.why: Both use spec_for to filter files and _IGNORE_DIRS to skip directories.

claims.text: Unlike ``_whole_repo_text``, dirnames ARE sorted here: this is new code with no prior byte-order contract to preserve, and BM25 tie-breaking needs a deterministic candidate order (see ``_bm25_context``).
claims.why: Code sorts dirnames before modifying list; _whole_repo_text does not sort dirnames.

claims.text: Standard k1=1.2 / b=0.75.
claims.why: Function signature has default k1=1.2, b=0.75.

claims.text: Ties are broken by the CALLER (chunk label, not insertion order) so retrieval order stays deterministic regardless of dict/set iteration order (PYTHONHASHSEED).
claims.why: _bm25_context sorts by (-score, label) to break ties deterministically.

claims.text: Chunks are taken whole, never split mid-chunk; the single best-ranked chunk is always included even if it alone exceeds budget (an empty context is a strictly worse baseline than a slightly-over one).
claims.why: Loop adds entire block; first chunk added unconditionally because picked is empty.

claims.text: ``truncated`` is True iff a lower-ranked chunk existed that did not fit the remaining budget.
claims.why: truncated set to True when a chunk is skipped due to budget; if all fit, remains False.

claims.text: A = the distilled semantic slice (today's product).
claims.why: semantic_slice function not in chunk.

claims.text: B = naive whole-repo concat. Recall is measured against the TRUE, FULL, UNTRUNCATED text (``tokens_B``) -- beating a baseline you truncated is not a win.
claims.why: Code calls _whole_repo_text(repo, cap_chars=None) for recall_B, count_tokens on full text.

claims.text: ``tokens_B_capped_at_default``/``b_truncated_at_cap`` additionally report what Tier 2 would actually hand a model (capped at ``_DEFAULT_MODEL_CAP_TOKENS``), so that weakening is visible, not hidden inside a smaller B that looks stronger than it is.
claims.why: tokens_B_capped_at_default and b_truncated_at_cap are not present in the returned dict in this chunk; may be added later.

claims.text: C = BM25 top-k retrieval, budgeted to the SAME token count as A (``token_budget_C == tokens_A``) -- the "dumb retrieval" baseline that matters commercially.
claims.why: budget_c = max(tokens_a, 1); _bm25_context called with budget_tokens=budget_c.

claims.text: ``c_beats_a`` is TIE-INCLUSIVE (``recall_C >= recall_A``, matching the report's "C>=A" column and this module's own docstring promise that a tie is "reported loudly, not smoothed over") and reported plainly either way; nothing here is tuned to make A win.
claims.why: c_beats_a not present in returned dict in this chunk; likely added later.

claims.text: NEVER RAISES: same per-task resolution guard as ``eval_task_tier1`` -- a ``ValueError``/``OSError`` resolving the repo or slicing the target returns an ERRORED row (``_task_error_row``) instead of propagating.
claims.why: Function wraps resolution and slicing in try/except ValueError/OSError; returns error row on exception.

claims.text: A CORRECTNESS task is likewise refused (``_correctness_task_row``) rather than scored: all three arms here go through ``_recall``, so a task with no ``must_include`` would read as a perfect 1.0 in every arm at once.
claims.why: First check is is_correctness_task, returns _correctness_task_row.

observations.what: Docstring for eval_task_arms mentions fields like tokens_B_capped_at_default, b_truncated_at_cap, c_beats_a that are not present in the returned dict in this chunk.
_whole_repo_text uses a character cap of _DEFAULT_MODEL_CAP_TOKENS * 4, but docstring does not explain multiplier.
Focus-withheld logic is referenced but not defined in this chunk; relies on _is_focus_withheld and _focus_withheld_row.
